text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition parties bury their differences at the last minute just for the sake of cooperation in the presidential elections.
- The United Nations-sponsored talks on Cyprus will be held under a news blackout.
- Right wing Disy and centre-right Diko parties are looking at the possibility of extending their present cooperation in the government to the upcoming presidential elections.
- Parliamentarians raise a special surcharge on electricity bills to give the Cyprus Broadcasting Corporation a boost.
- Opposition parties strike deal on programme to back Nicosia lawyer Marios Eliades in the presidential elections.
- Opposition parties reach agreement for cooperation in the presidential elections.
- The United Nations are keeping their cards close to their chest on the upcoming talks in New York between President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
- Opposition parties reach agreement on Marios (Eliades) standing as their common candidate in the elections.
- Gyms and hairdressing salons are supplying clients with dangerous pills which induce weight loss. The pills were illegally imported to Cyprus.
- Parliament is due to discuss Cyprus's attempts to combat money laundering next week.

- Leaders of Communist Akel, socialist Edek and the centre-left United Democrats party made the incompatible compatible, agreeing to cooperate in the presidential elections because they did not want to take on the burden of a possible failure.
